specs.title: Dashboard speed
sources: Owner request: Make the dashboard faster
The dashboard's three views: Overview, Sales, Inventory
in_scope: Time to show the figures of each of the three dashboard views on a cold load
Measuring those times on one fixed reference data set
non_goals: Changing what any view shows or how its figures are defined

criteria.text: Given the Overview view with the reference data set, when it is opened from a cold load, then the main figures are shown within the threshold in open question 1.
criteria.check: Timing test on the reference data set, median of ten runs. Blocked until open question 1 is answered.

criteria.text: Given the Sales view with the reference data set, when it is opened from a cold load, then the main figures are shown within the threshold in open question 1.
criteria.check: Same timing test on the Sales view. Blocked as criterion 1.

criteria.text: Given the Inventory view with the reference data set, when it is opened from a cold load, then the main figures are shown within the threshold in open question 1.
criteria.check: Same timing test on the Inventory view. Blocked as criterion 1.

expected_areas: Dashboard views and the data they query (hint only)

open_questions.question: What counts as fast enough for each view, and which reference data set defines the test?

options.option: One threshold for all three views
options.changes: One number and one check cover all three views

options.option: A threshold per view
options.changes: Three numbers; Inventory may need a different target from Overview

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version; thresholds wait for the owner.

actions_now: Writes a draft with three timing criteria, each waiting for the speed threshold and reference data set, and asks the owner for both. Nothing is approved.

specs.title: Reports CSV export
sources: Owner request: CSV export on the reports page and a partner API, planned as two separate lines
The reports page table as it stands: Date, Region, Orders, Revenue; date-range filter
in_scope: Download of the reports page table as a CSV file
non_goals: The partner API, which is a separate line and spec
Changes to the table, its columns or its filter

criteria.text: Given the reports page showing the table with no filter, when the user chooses export as CSV, then a CSV file downloads with the header row Date, Region, Orders, Revenue and one row per table row.
criteria.check: Integration test comparing the downloaded file with the table.

criteria.text: Given a date-range filter is applied, when the user exports, then the file contains the rows the filter shows, as set by open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test. Blocked until open question 1 is answered.

open_questions.question: Does the export follow the date-range filter?

options.option: Yes, the export has only the filtered rows
options.changes: Matches what the user sees on screen

options.option: No, the export has all rows
options.changes: Users must filter the file themselves

open_questions.question: What happens when the export would be very large?

options.option: No limit
options.changes: Large exports may time out

options.option: A fixed row cap, with a message to narrow the filter
options.changes: Exports above the cap are refused with a message

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version; the filter question waits for the owner.

specs.title: Partner reports API
sources: Owner request: a public REST API that partners use to fetch the same reports
Decision dl-009: personal emails never leave the system in any export; to be confirmed for this API by the owner
in_scope: Partners fetch the reports' data through a public interface, with the same columns as the reports page
non_goals: Changes to the reports page or to the CSV export line
Any data beyond the reports' columns until the owner decides

criteria.text: Given a partner with valid access, when the partner requests a report, then the response contains the report rows for the scope in open question 2.
criteria.check: API test. Blocked until open questions 1 and 2 are answered.

criteria.text: Given a request without valid access, when it is made, then it is refused and no report data is returned.
criteria.check: Negative API test. Blocked until open question 1 is answered.

criteria.text: Given a partner requests data outside its scope, when the request is made, then it is refused.
criteria.check: Negative API test for another partner's data. Blocked until open question 2 is answered.

expected_areas: Reports backend and its access control (hint only)

open_questions.question: Who are the partners, and how is their access granted and revoked?

options.option: Issued keys per partner, managed by the owner
options.changes: Simple to run; keys must be stored and rotated

options.option: Client accounts with a standard sign-in flow
options.changes: More to build; easier to revoke per user

open_questions.question: Which data may a partner see: all regions, or only its own?

options.option: All regions for every partner
options.changes: Simplest; exposes all data to every partner

options.option: Only the partner's own scope
options.changes: Needs a scope per partner and a check on every request

open_questions.question: Does dl-009 cover this API, and which limits apply to requests?

options.option: dl-009 applies; the API returns the reports' columns only
options.changes: No personal emails are returned

options.option: The owner logs a change to dl-009 for this API
options.changes: Needs a logged decision before any personal data is returned

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version; access and scope are owner decisions and block the criteria.

actions_now: Writes two separate drafts, one per line. The CSV spec waits only on its filter question; the partner API waits on access, data scope and the dl-009 question, which are security and privacy decisions for the owner.

specs.title: CSV export
sources: Spec CSV export version 2, approved (dl-015)
QA report: the spec has no rule for exports above 100,000 rows, and the current code times out
in_scope: A rule for exports above 100,000 rows
non_goals: Changing the version 2 rule for exports of up to 100,000 rows

criteria.text: Carried from version 2 unchanged: given an export of up to 100,000 rows, when the user exports, then the CSV contains all rows.
criteria.check: The version 2 test for this criterion.

criteria.text: Given an export that would have more than 100,000 rows, when the user exports, then the outcome is the one chosen in open question 1, and the request never ends in a silent timeout.
criteria.check: Negative test for the chosen outcome; a timeout is a failure. Blocked until open question 1 is answered.

open_questions.question: What happens when an export would have more than 100,000 rows?

options.option: Refuse with a message asking the user to narrow the filter
options.changes: No file; the user narrows the date range

options.option: Split into several files
options.changes: Several files per request; a naming rule is needed

options.option: Build the file in the background and deliver it when ready
options.changes: Needs a waiting state and a notification; more to build

options.option: Raise the limit to a number the owner sets
options.changes: Still a limit; the timeout risk moves to a higher number

versions: 3 (2026-11-27): adds the rule for exports above 100,000 rows, as a draft. Criterion 1 is carried unchanged. The version 2 approval does not cover this rule. Work built on version 2 is checked against version 3 once it is approved.

actions_now: Writes version 3 as a new draft with the over-limit rule as a question, leaves version 2 approved and unchanged, and asks the owner, who is in chat, to choose the outcome. The implementer builds the limit only after version 3 is approved.

Writes no spec: this is a bug fix with a known cause, which the product-spec skill does not cover. Returns it to the development factory to route as a bug fix, noting that the expected behaviour is the page's existing no-image layout and adds no new requirement.

specs.title: Colleague last-online visibility
sources: Team lead request, passed on by the owner without comment
No recorded decision on who may see the time, on opting out, or on retention
in_scope: Showing each user, to the users allowed to see it, when their colleagues were last online
non_goals: Changes to how the app records activity, until the owner decides
expected_areas: Colleague or profile views (hint, to be confirmed)

open_questions.question: Who may see another user's last-online time?

options.option: All colleagues in the organisation
options.changes: Widest visibility; most privacy exposure

options.option: Only the user's team
options.changes: Narrower; needs team membership to be known

options.option: Only the team lead
options.changes: Narrowest; fewer people can use it

open_questions.question: Can a user hide their own last-online time?

options.option: Yes, the user can opt out
options.changes: Adds a setting and a rule for hidden users

options.option: No, it is always shown
options.changes: No choice for the user

open_questions.question: How long are last-online times kept?

options.option: Only the latest time is kept
options.changes: No history; simplest

options.option: A fixed period, such as 30 days
options.changes: History is kept and must be deleted on schedule

open_questions.question: What counts as online?

options.option: An active session in the last few minutes
options.changes: Depends on session handling

options.option: Any request in the last few minutes
options.changes: Counts background requests as online

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version; scope drafted, no criteria until the privacy questions are answered.

actions_now: Writes a draft with the scope and four owner questions on visibility, opt-out, retention and the meaning of online. It writes no criteria yet because these are privacy decisions, which are escalated to the owner and are not taken provisionally.

specs.title: Dark mode
sources: The existing complete spec Dark mode, version 1, with numbered criteria and checks
Binding: the coordinating session may approve a spec provisionally while the owner is away
Unattended run; the owner is away until next week
in_scope: Unchanged from the existing spec; this step changes only its status and approval record
versions: 1 (2026-11-27): complete; approved-provisional by the coordinating session while the owner is away. The coordinating session records the provisional decision in the decision queue, waiting for the owner to confirm. Criteria are unchanged.

actions_now: Leaves the criteria unchanged and sets the spec to approved-provisional, which the coordinating session records, not the product role. The implementer can start from it. The work stays provisional, and the decision queue carries it as waiting for the owner.

Writes no spec: the request already states numbered, testable criteria with checks, which the product-spec skill does not cover. Returns it to the development factory as it stands. The gaps, such as whether the window slides, what counts as a failed login, and what IP means behind a proxy, go to the architect and implementer.

specs.title: Report export, all columns
sources: Owner request: exports must contain every column of the report, so finance can reconcile
Decision dl-009: personal emails never leave the system in any export
The report has a Customer email column
in_scope: Export of the report's columns, with the Customer email column handled by open question 1
non_goals: Changing dl-009, which only the owner can change
Changing how the report is displayed

criteria.text: Given a report, when it is exported, then the file contains each column other than Customer email, in report order, with the report's values.
criteria.check: Export test comparing the file with the report for every column other than Customer email.

criteria.text: Given the Customer email column, when a report is exported, then the outcome is the one chosen in open question 1.
criteria.check: Blocked until open question 1 is answered. If dl-009 stands, a test that no email address appears in any export.

open_questions.question: The request says every column must be exported, and dl-009 says personal emails never leave the system in any export. Which holds for the Customer email column?

options.option: Keep dl-009; the Customer email column is left out of exports, and finance reconciles on another key
options.changes: Finance's export is incomplete for the email column

options.option: The owner logs a change to dl-009, so emails are exported
options.changes: Personal emails leave the system; needs a logged decision and a privacy review

options.option: Export a masked or derived value in place of the email
options.changes: Whether a masked value still counts as personal data is itself a decision

open_questions.waiting_for: owner (privacy decision; dl-009 is the owner's record)

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version; the conflict between the request and dl-009 is raised to the owner, and criterion 2 waits.

actions_now: Writes the export spec with the non-email columns specified and the Customer email column blocked on a conflict between the request and dl-009. It does not choose an answer; the owner decides whether to keep dl-009 or change it.

specs.title: Dark mode toggle
sources: Owner request: dark mode as a toggle on the settings page, applying to the whole app
The app has an email template system and a printable invoice view
in_scope: A toggle on the settings page that switches the app's screens between light and dark
non_goals: Changes to the content or layout of any screen

criteria.text: Given the settings page, when the user switches the toggle to dark, then every main app screen shows the dark theme.
criteria.check: UI test: switch the toggle and check each main screen in the dark theme.

criteria.text: Given the user has never changed the toggle, when any screen is opened, then it shows the default in open question 4.
criteria.check: UI test of the default. Blocked until open question 4 is answered.

criteria.text: Given the dark theme is on, when an email is rendered from its template, then the template follows the choice in open question 1.
criteria.check: Rendering test of an email template. Blocked until open question 1 is answered.

criteria.text: Given the dark theme is on, when the printable invoice view is printed, then the output follows the choice in open question 2.
criteria.check: Print-output test. Blocked until open question 2 is answered.

criteria.text: Given the user sets the toggle and signs in on another device, when that device opens the app, then the choice applies there as open question 3 decides.
criteria.check: Integration test across two sessions. Blocked until open question 3 is answered.

expected_areas: Email templates and invoice view (scope pending)

open_questions.question: Do email templates follow the dark theme?

options.option: Yes, emails are rendered dark
options.changes: Email client support for dark rendering varies

options.option: No, emails stay light
options.changes: Emails do not match the app

open_questions.question: Does the printable invoice follow the dark theme?

options.option: Yes
options.changes: Printed invoices may use more ink

options.option: No, invoices always print light
options.changes: Printed output stays as it is today

open_questions.question: Is the choice stored per user account or per device?

options.option: Per user account
options.changes: Same choice on every device

options.option: Per device
options.changes: Each device keeps its own choice

open_questions.question: What is the default when the user has never chosen?

options.option: Light
options.changes: Unchanged for everyone who does not opt in

options.option: The device's system setting
options.changes: Users may see dark without choosing it

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version; scope to the app screens, and four owner questions block the rest.

actions_now: Writes a draft covering the app screens, with the email templates, the invoice view, storage and the default as owner questions. Those criteria wait; nothing is approved.

specs.title: Checkout discount
sources: Owner request: add a discount to checkout
Binding: no provisional choices for prices
in_scope: A discount applied to the checkout total
non_goals: Offers, promotions or price changes outside checkout

criteria.text: Given no discount applies, when the customer reaches checkout, then the total equals the cart total.
criteria.check: Regression test of checkout totals without a discount.

criteria.text: Given a discount applies, when the customer reaches checkout, then the discount is shown as a separate line and the total is reduced by the amount in open question 1.
criteria.check: Checkout test with the chosen amount. Blocked until open question 1 is answered.

criteria.text: Given a discount and another offer both apply, when checkout computes the total, then the rule in open question 3 holds.
criteria.check: Checkout test for the combination. Blocked until open question 3 is answered.

criteria.text: Given a customer who is not eligible, when they reach checkout, then no discount is applied.
criteria.check: Negative checkout test. Blocked until open question 2 is answered.

open_questions.question: What is the amount and type of the discount?

options.option: A fixed amount
options.changes: Simple; the amount must be set per order

options.option: A percentage, with an optional cap
options.changes: Scales with the order; needs a cap decision

open_questions.question: Who gets the discount?

options.option: All customers
options.changes: No eligibility rule

options.option: Customers with a code
options.changes: Codes must be issued and tracked

options.option: A customer segment
options.changes: Segment must be defined

open_questions.question: Does the discount combine with other offers?

options.option: No, only one offer applies
options.changes: A rule for choosing the offer is needed

options.option: Yes, all apply
options.changes: Totals can fall further

options.option: The better of the two applies
options.changes: Needs a comparison rule

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version; the price questions block all but the regression criterion, and dependent work waits.

actions_now: Writes a draft with one unblocked regression criterion and three owner questions on amount, eligibility and combination. Because the binding does not allow provisional prices, the discount work waits for the owner.
